column3: A tall tower with eight sections that recall a stalk of bamboo, once the tallest building in the world. A huge steel ball inside it steadies the tower in typhoons.
A museum with hundreds of thousands of imperial treasures, including jade, bronzes and paintings, that were moved from Beijing in the 1940s. A carved jade cabbage is among the favorites.
A white hall with a blue roof, set in a large square with gardens, with a hall that houses a statue of Chiang Kai-shek and a guard-changing ceremony.
A temple in Taipei that is a center of folk faith, where worshippers burn incense to many gods, with carved dragons on the roof.
The largest night market in Taipei, with food stalls, games and shops. You can sample fried chicken, oyster omelets and sweet drinks until late.
A hillside town of old mining streets, tea houses and red lanterns, with views of the sea, said to have inspired a famous animated film.
A wide waterfall, called Taiwan's Niagara, near a railway town where people release sky lanterns.
A harbor town at the mouth of the Tamsui River, with an old street of snacks and a sunset view over the water.
A national park above Taipei with hot springs, flower fields and volcanic hills, which is spectacular in cherry blossom season.
A pedestrian area of youth culture, with cinemas, shops, street performers and snacks.
A hot spring district with steaming valleys, old bathhouses and a museum, a place to unwind in a warm bath.
A bowl of beef noodle soup with chunks of braised beef in a spicy or clear broth. It is the island's unofficial national dish, with a yearly competition.
Soup dumplings made famous by a shop in Taipei. Thin-skinned and filled with broth, they are eaten with ginger and vinegar.
Pork stewed in soy sauce and served over rice, a classic comfort food with a rich, sweet and savory taste.
Milk tea with chewy tapioca pearls, first made in Taiwan in the 1980s. It is drunk through a wide straw, and has become popular around the world.
Fermented tofu fried until crisp, with a very strong smell and a savory flavor, served with pickled cabbage and chili.
A starchy omelet with small oysters, egg and greens, topped with sweet and spicy sauce, a night market favorite.
A shortbread pastry with pineapple jam, a Taiwanese gift that visitors take home.
Fried chicken bites with salt, pepper and basil, a night market snack.
Mountains of shaved ice with toppings such as mango, beans and condensed milk, a cool treat for summer.
A giant fried chicken cutlet, bigger than a face, sprinkled with pepper, and eaten from a paper bag as you stroll.
Glove puppetry, in which small, beautifully dressed puppets are moved by the hand, and act out martial-arts dramas.
Taiwanese opera, which grew out of folk songs, has love stories and heroic tales told in the Hokkien language.
Paper lanterns with wishes written on them are released into the sky, and carry hopes and prayers.
The Ghost Festival in the seventh lunar month, when families make offerings of food and burn paper money for ancestors and wandering spirits.
Two seven-story pagodas shaped like a dragon and a tiger stand by Lotus Pond. You enter through the dragon's mouth and exit through the tiger's for good luck.
A large Buddhist monastery with a huge Buddha statue and many halls, with a museum and vegetarian food.
A narrow island with seafood restaurants, a beach and a lighthouse, a short ferry ride from Kaohsiung.
A famous night market in Kaohsiung, with seafood, papaya milk, grilled meat and other snacks.
A subway station with a huge glass dome, the Dome of Light, among the most beautiful in the world.
A sweet drink of papaya and milk, blended until it is smooth, a Kaohsiung favorite.
Mullet roe that is salted, dried and grilled, and is thinly sliced and eaten with garlic and radish, a delicacy.
A small bowl of noodles with a savory sauce, shrimp and minced pork, a snack that first started with fishermen.
Thick toast hollowed out and filled with a creamy seafood or chicken stew, a Tainan invention.
A building from the Dutch era with a Chinese-style roof, which was once the seat of Dutch rule in Tainan.
A fort built by the Dutch in the 17th century, with brick walls, and a view of the old harbor of Anping.
The first Confucius temple in Taiwan, built in 1665, in a quiet garden of old trees.
An old lane of old merchant houses, with lanterns, cafés and small shops, which is especially lovely in the evening.
A well-known noodle shop in Tainan that has been selling its small bowls of noodles since 1895.
A morning hot beef soup made with thin slices of fresh beef poured over with hot broth, a Tainan breakfast.
Egg noodles stir-fried with eel in a sweet-sour sauce, a Tainan specialty.
A porridge with milkfish, a typical Tainan breakfast, with a light flavor.
A military dependents' village painted by a former soldier in bright colors and patterns, now an art spot.
A tidal flat where the sunset reflects on shallow water, with windmills and birds on the horizon.
A big night market near a university in Taichung, known for creative snacks and cheap fashion.
A flaky pastry with a sweet malt filling, a Taichung specialty and a popular gift.
A marble canyon with cliff paths and tunnels cut into the rock, where a river has carved a deep gorge through the mountains. It is the best-known natural sight on the east coast.
A long valley of rice fields and farms between two mountain ranges, with a slow rhythm of country life.
Chewy rice cakes rolled in peanut or sesame powder, a Hualien specialty.
Wonton soup with thin skins and a clear broth, a local classic in Hualien.
The largest Indigenous people on the east coast, known for their songs, dances and their harvest festivals.
A harvest festival of the Amis people, with singing, dancing and a feast to thank the ancestors.
A lake in the mountains, with a shape that looks like a sun on one side and a moon on the other. A cycling path circles the lake, and boats cross the water.
A mountain known for a sunrise above a sea of clouds, giant old cypress trees and a small mountain train.
The highest mountain in Taiwan, at about 3,950 meters, whose summit is reached by a long hike.
A high-mountain farm with grasslands and sheep, with views of the mountains and a European feel.
A tea grown at high altitude, where cool, misty weather gives it a sweet, smooth taste.
A well-known oolong from the slopes of Alishan, with a floral aroma and a mellow taste.
A small Indigenous people who live around Sun Moon Lake, with their own language and customs.
Scallions grown in the fertile soil of Sanxing in Yilan, thicker and sweeter than most.
Fried pork rolls, crisp outside and juicy inside, a local snack in Yilan.
An island off the southeast coast, home of the Tao people, with traditional boats and flying fish festivals.
The sugar apple is a sweet, creamy fruit with a bumpy green skin, a Taitung specialty.
A famous railway lunchbox of rice, pork and pickles, which is sold at Chishang station.
An island people of Orchid Island, known for their flying fish traditions and their carved boats.
A beach and national park at the southern tip of the island, with coral reefs, a lighthouse and a lively beach town.
A sweet, crisp, dark red fruit, a Pingtung specialty known as the black pearl wax apple.
A famous braised pork knuckle, cooked slowly in soy sauce, from Wanluan.
Thin rice noodles dried in the wind of Hsinchu, which are stir-fried with mushrooms, meat and dried shrimp.
A bouncy pork meatball, often served in soup, a Hsinchu favorite.
A fried sandwich from Keelung's night market with tomato, ham, cucumber and a sweet sauce.
Keelung's fried fish cake is soft and chewy, and is served with sweet sauce, a local street snack.
A strong sorghum liquor made on Kinmen, which is famous in Taiwan and often sold as a gift.
A peanut candy that is crumbly and sweet, and a Kinmen specialty.
